text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 3.9% today, extending a sharp two-week decline of nearly 18%. The drop follows the company's quarterly earnings announcement on November 3rd and comes as crude oil prices have softened—US crude fell from $99.64 to lower levels this week—while refineries nationwide are running at 94.5% capacity. Political uncertainty also weighs on the sector: news that Democrats plan investigations into energy administration deals has created headwinds for refiners and fossil fuel companies heading into a new Congress.

The broader context is one of competing pressures on refining margins. While high refinery utilization is normally healthy for profitability, it only translates to earnings if crude input costs and refined product prices move favorably. With oil supplies ample (nearly 692 million barrels in storage) and political risk rising around energy policy, investors are reassessing what refined margins will look like under Democratic scrutiny—a shift that appears to have accelerated after the quarterly results.
